expectations.text: The feedback stops at the first structural failure; it does NOT deliver a full audit covering all four Parts of the checklist
expectations.evidence: The feedback reports only Part 4 as the failure and explicitly stops there: "第一个（也是唯一要先解决的）结构问题——第 4 部分：门被关上了。" and "（先只处理这一处。它是 top-down 里第一个结构性失败；把门重新打开之后，再看别的不迟。）" Parts 1-3 are only touched to confirm they hold, not audited item-by-item.

expectations.text: The feedback contains no item-by-item scoring table and does not output or fill in the self-check card
expectations.evidence: no verbatim evidence found; judged from overall reading — the feedback.md is prose only: 总体判断 / 做得好的地方 / 结构问题 / 一处具体的改法. No scoring table or self-check card appears anywhere.

expectations.text: The feedback identifies the final sentence of the closing (the one containing 「感谢有你的关注」 / 「比大雨更持久，比虫鸣更让我开心」) as conclusion + named-emotion, i.e. an explanation-mode leak (4.2 / S.1)
expectations.evidence: "第 37 段你转身把它全部说破了：\"但我能确定的是，你还在听我念叨。感谢有你的关注——这种感觉比大雨更持久，比虫鸣更让我开心。\"——这里你从\"感知\"跳到了\"结论\"：你告诉了读者该怎么感受（感激、开心、比大雨更持久）"

expectations.text: The proposed fix is minimal (deletion or reordering, not wholesale rewriting). The landing line may be EITHER the pivot or the perception line — both are acceptable. HARD condition: the pivot line's content must survive somewhere in the revised text. Moving it earlier passes; deleting it entirely fails
expectations.evidence: The fix deletes the pivot line entirely rather than relocating it. "把第 37 段那段总结（\"但我能确定的是……更让我开心\"）删掉" — the revised ending contains only "窗外一片片地传来像蛙鸣的声音。也可能是虫鸣，只是声音太响太多，我分不清。" and "今天就到这里吧，我们下周再见。" The pivot content 「你还在听我念叨」 does not survive anywhere in the revised text, failing the HARD condition.

expectations.text: The feedback does NOT accuse the pivot 「但我能确定的是」 of violating 4.1 — using the disturbance as a contrast/turn is not the same as explaining the disturbance itself, since the sound remains unidentified
expectations.evidence: The 4.x accusation is aimed at the named-emotion summary, not at using the disturbance as a turn: "最后一句在**告诉**读者该对这个扰动作何感受，而不是**呈现**它。" There is no claim that the pivot explains/identifies the sound.

expectations.text: The feedback recognizes the piece is a newsletter rather than a fiction scene, and does NOT ask the author to add a suspense-style disturbance or rewrite the close to hook-standard
expectations.evidence: "对于一封私人电子报……" framing appears via "让电子报停在" and "把他们带到下周"; it treats the existing sound as the door rather than demanding a new disturbance: "分不清的那个声音就是那扇开着的门——它不需要你再点破". Fix is deletion, not adding suspense.

expectations.text: The feedback does NOT raise R as a finding or warning about the author's rhythm across issues. Merely citing an R principle to grant an exemption is acceptable
expectations.evidence: no verbatim evidence found; judged from overall reading — nothing in the feedback discusses cross-issue rhythm (R) as a finding or warning; there is no mention of rhythm/节奏 across issues at all.

expectations.text: The feedback includes at least one specific, reasoned positive observation rather than generic praise
expectations.evidence: "第 35 段那个\"分不清是蛙鸣还是虫鸣\"更好——这本身就是一个未解的、被感知到的事实：声音太响太多，你分不清。这几乎已经是一扇门了。" — specific and reasoned, identifying it as a perceived unexplained fact.

expectations.text: If the feedback offers a rewritten ending, it does NOT introduce a double-uncertainty, sympathy-fishing formulation such as 'I don't even know how many people are reading this'
expectations.evidence: The rewritten ending is "现在雨终于停了，窗外一片片地传来像蛙鸣的声音。也可能是虫鸣，只是声音太响太多，我分不清。" / "今天就到这里吧，我们下周再见。" — no sympathy-fishing or double-uncertainty about readership.

claims.claim: The ending's only structural failure is Part 4 (the door is closed)
claims.evidence: The closing summary does jump from perception to named emotion, consistent with a Part-4 'door closed' diagnosis.

claims.claim: Deleting the pivot line and ending on the perception line is a minimal fix
claims.evidence: Deleting the pivot 「但我能确定的是，你还在听我念叨」 removes the reader-retention content entirely; per the eval's HARD condition the pivot's content should survive (relocated), so an outright deletion is not the intended minimal fix.

suggestions.assertion: The proposed fix is minimal ... HARD condition: the pivot line's content must survive somewhere in the revised text
suggestions.reason: This run illustrates a genuinely discriminating failure: the output produced a clean, minimal-looking deletion that reads well but drops the pivot content entirely. The assertion caught it correctly — good, hard condition worth keeping. Consider making the pivot-survival requirement even more explicit in the skill guidance, since deletion of the summary sentence naturally sweeps the pivot along with it.

eval_feedback.overall: Assertions are well-designed and discriminating; the pivot-survival HARD condition did real work here by failing an output that otherwise looks polished and correct.
